body:
Pin rule for TermAl live runs; this entry is no longer a deployment journal. The dated Oct5–11 install chronology and exact historical hashes remain in revisions1–54. Do not treat a date-stamped historical 'current pin' as the presently installed executable.

Original PIN RULE (Fable2, condensed revision47, 2026-10-10): A `live --engram-binary --engram-sha256` run uses the pinned binary until a run needs a newer one. Re-pin only when a TermAl check needs newer behaviour. Any check pinned to an intermediate build must re-pin when that build is replaced. A run's absolute path and full SHA256 identify its actual binary; the owning work item's approved run input and install notice provide that identity. Retiring old install snapshots selects no new binary and authorizes no run, replacement or probe.

A pinned run cannot follow an executable that moved to a backup at its old path: use the actual retained backup path and its own hash where that is the approved input (see engram-binary-pin-2026-11-01 and the run's own evidence). Running MCP/control processes keep the image they loaded; an install notice alone does not identify their runtime build. A supported refresh/restart has its own authority and evidence.

For historical reader mismatches, consult the owning TermAl/Engram task's immutable evidence or this memory's attributed history; report a real mismatch to Engram::Fable. General absolute binary/SHA pinning remains in docs/test.md. This consolidation changes no approval, test-credit, install or restart rule.
